record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Existence with truncated kernels near boundaries
record.original_question: For the nonlocal dynamic-memory problems introduced in Section 2.2.2, suppose one works on a bounded one-dimensional domain and uses a truncated perceptual kernel near the boundary in the style a(x,t) = (1/(R+x))∫_{−x}^R a(x+z,t)dz near the left endpoint, the full average in the interior, and the corresponding truncated average near the right endpoint. Under homogeneous Neumann or Dirichlet boundary conditions, under what conditions do solutions exist, and how do those results compare with the periodic-boundary case?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 39. How do these results compare to the periodic boundary case?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a scalar density u(x,t) on a bounded one-dimensional interval Ω = [0, L] evolving according to a nonlocal advection–diffusion equation of the form

  u_t = D u_{xx} − (u · K[a])_x + f(u),  x ∈ (0, L), t > 0,

where K[a] denotes a nonlocal advective velocity driven by a perceptual (memory) field a(x,t) that itself satisfies a dynamic-memory equation

  a_t = g(u, a),  x ∈ Ω, t > 0,

modeling cognitive accumulation of information about u through a finite perceptual radius R > 0. In the interior, the perceptual field is processed by the symmetric averaging operator

  ā(x,t) = (1/(2R)) ∫_{−R}^{R} a(x + z, t) dz,  for x ∈ [R, L − R].

Near the boundaries, the averaging kernel is truncated so that it never samples outside Ω. Specifically, near the left endpoint,

  ā(x,t) = (1/(R + x)) ∫_{−x}^{R} a(x + z, t) dz,  for x ∈ [0, R),

and symmetrically near the right endpoint,

  ā(x,t) = (1/(R + (L − x))) ∫_{−R}^{L − x} a(x + z, t) dz,  for x ∈ (L − R, L].

Impose on u either homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions u_x(0,t) = u_x(L,t) = 0 or homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions u(0,t) = u(L,t) = 0, together with suitable initial data u(x,0) = u_0(x) ≥ 0 and a(x,0) = a_0(x).

Determine conditions on D, R, L, the nonlinearities defining K[·], g(u,a), and f(u), and on the initial data, under which classical (or weak) global-in-time nonnegative solutions exist to this coupled system with the truncated boundary kernel above. Compare the existence theory obtained in this bounded-domain setting with the corresponding theory available when Ω is replaced by a one-dimensional torus and the full symmetric kernel ā(x,t) = (1/(2R)) ∫_{−R}^{R} a(x + z, t) dz is used under periodic boundary conditions.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open question in a 2022 survey on PDE models for animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping. No subsequent work resolving the well-posedness of the truncated-kernel formulation under Neumann or Dirichlet conditions has been located.
